newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks firm from open after Dow bounce.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks firm from open after Dow bounce.

text.p: Australian shares opened modestly firmer on Tuesday as investors factored in the effects of a solid gain from the Wall Street market, which bounced on some solid earnings reports following Friday's steep sell-off.
At 10.15 a.m. (0015 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was up 10.6 points at 2,376.7.
The June share price index was up 10 points at 2,366 and at a 10.7 point discount to the underlying index.
Most blue chip issues gained a few cents early in the session although trading activity remained very quiet. Resources were slightly favoured over industrials.

"After yesterday, the market has again taken its lead from Wall Street but investors are sitting on the sidelines due to the CPI figure due out in the U.S. tonight," said Peter Struk, a dealer at Sydney brokerage, Reynolds & Co.

Struk said that after Wall Street's sharp negative reaction to a rise in wholesale prices on Friday, local investors were reluctant to trade of another potential volatile session for the Dow later today.
"Our market is not going to do anything foolish today so I would suggest that if it finishes five or 10 points up on the day it has done reasonably well," he said.
With the exception of a couple of small sectors, stocks opened up across the board with the resources sector bolstered by modest rises from the Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd and CRA Ltd.
The major banks were also modestly higher with the exception of the largest, National Australia Bank Ltd which opened slightly weaker before edging into positive territory.
One strong issue was QBE Insurance Ltd whose shares were up 16 cents to A$6.56 (US$5.12) in early trade, regaining the fall it made on Monday following the Dow's 148 point slide on Friday.
